messages:
laura: Heads-up — planning a terraform apply for the vpc-routing change in tonight's change window (2026-11-10 20:00 UTC). Please DO NOT merge PRs touching infra/modules/network until preflight + apply-lock are cleared. PR: https://git.internal/r/redwood/infra/pull/842

mike: Ack, holding my DB-subnet PR. Are we pinning any provider or module versions for this roll?

laura: Yes — provider pinned to aws v4.58.0 in the PR. Also gating on provider-unit tests and the plan sanity check. Deploy-bot will post the plan shortly.

deploy-bot: Preflight started for PR #842. Plan URL: https://ci.internal/builds/29823/plan
Lock status: apply-lock=ACQUIRED by laura. ETA for plan completion ~ 8m.

laura: Plan summary (excerpt):
```
# terraform plan summary
+ aws_route.rtb_public: 3 to add
~ aws_vpc_peering.peer: 1 to update
No destroys detected
```

arik: If routes change, can we canary apply in us-west-2 first? I suggest regional order: us-west-2 -> us-east-1 -> eu-west-1. That reduces blast radius.

laura: Agreed. We'll run a regional canary apply. I will manually trigger the canary once approvals are in. If the canary fails, we'll auto-fallback to the prior route config and abort the rest.

mike: Quick note on rollback: revert the PR branch, re-run apply with previous route table IDs (runbook updated here: https://wiki.internal/runbooks/infra-routing-rollback). Also keep BGP advertisements disabled until we verify.

infra-bot: Change window noted: 2026-11-10 20:00-21:00 UTC. Canary flag enabled. Auto-fallback policy configured to 'previous-config' on apply error >= 5% error rate or >60s median latency.

sre-oncall: I'll be watching canary metrics and will silence noisy alerts. Ping me if error rate > 1% or p50 latency jumps > 50ms.

laura: Final operational ask: hold any non-network merges (dependabot, infra formatting) out of infra/* until after full rollout. We'll update release notes with the exact rollout timeline and canary verdict once complete. :thumbsup:
